tokens.v: Read the matte-black anodised device with the milled edges, machined side vent and knurled control that follows as this silver-top-plate rangefinder camera instead, and let the bench work on it: the dial indicator's chrome stand has been walked in until its plunger sits down on the top plate just behind the empty hot shoe, the needle a third off zero on a plain unnumbered face. 80mm at f/11 from forty-five degrees above the granite, thirty centimetres out and square to the grid, so the whole top plate opens up without collapsing the body — both knurled dials, the concentric collar switch at the right dial's base and the round finder window all read, the fixed prime pointing camera-left with one bright line along its milled aperture ring. Body about two-thirds of the frame width at true palm scale, its base plate flat to the lapped granite with a hard contact shadow and no gap. FIELDNOTE is engraved and paint-filled in clean capitals across the top plate, large and easily read. The wrung gauge-block stack stands tack sharp at frame-left, its corner cutting the bottom edge.
